en: The Mañjuśrī-parinirvāṇa-nāma-dharmaparyāya,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Mingyin Miaoshan Pujie of the Western Heaven (India) during the Song Dynasty,
along with Jin Zongchi and others, by imperial decree.
Homage to Mañjuśrī, who expounds the most supreme meaning;
to the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, who subdues the hosts of Māras,
whose body surges forth pervading the three realms, and who is the sovereign King of Secrets.
With eyes like blue lotus petals and a face like a blooming lotus,
he grasps a vajra, hurling it again and again with his hand;
manifesting a form of great wrath, his majesty shakes the worlds of the ten directions.
The Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi also holds a vajra;
his appearance of diligence is subtle and wondrous. With valor he subdues all māras, and with great wisdom he benefits all sentient beings, manifesting as hundreds of millions of vajras.
Some leap for joy, while others manifest wrathful forms;
they prostrate to the Buddha, the World-Honored One. With palms joined in reverence, they pray that the Dharma may endure for a long time and that he may serve as the refuge for all sentient beings.
Constantly within the net of illusion, you lead [beings] onto the path to enlightenment;
for those who are ignorant, deluded, and afflicted by suffering and afflictions,
you provide protection and liberation, guarding them all toward the supreme fruit.
The World-Honored One, the Teacher who Subdues, Ever abiding in the Great Samādhi, Is able to comprehend the nature of all phenomena; The faculties and their objects are likewise so.
The Tathāgata’s body of wisdom Bears the mark of the *uṣṇīṣa*.
Mañjuśrī, the Great Wise One, through his wisdom-contemplation,
excellently brings forth the most profound and subtle meaning; this Great Dharma is peerless,
excellent in the beginning, middle, and end, and its name and meaning are supreme.
The Buddhas of the past have already spoken; the Buddhas of the future shall speak; the Buddhas of the present speak now.
Thus it is in all three times within the great net of illusion, able to deliver all classes of beings.
The Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, with joy, offers this praise:
"The Buddha has spoken these true secret words; I am now able to receive and uphold them, With a resolute mind made firm, until the attainment of Equal and Perfect Enlightenment."
Proclaiming the secret Dharma, he guides all sentient beings to give rise to untainted wisdom; with his afflictions exhausted without remainder,
the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi stands before the Buddha with palms joined.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha, the supreme among two-legged beings,
with his tongue of truthful speech and pure, wondrous voice,
caused it to flow throughout the world; thus, the four kinds of Māras did not appear.
Pervading throughout the three realms, with a Brahma-voice you offer beautiful praise;
To the Tathāgata Guhyarāja, you proclaim the essential points of the Great Dharma.
Excellent, O Vajrapāṇi! Excellent, O Vajrahasta!
For the sake of bringing benefit, may the one of great wisdom who has attained the supreme and ultimate purpose,
the Great Sage Mañjuśrī who eradicates all stains of sin, please listen to this meaning.
Excellent, O Great Guide! You have skillfully proclaimed this teaching.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha revealed the secret dharma, which upholds the great vidyā-mantras—namely, the Vidyādhara-piṭaka.
The Mundane and Supramundane Section; the Section on the Universal World;
the Section on the Great Seals and All Dharmas; the Section on the Uṣṇīṣa;
the Sixfold Great Kings of Mantras—these are in accord and non-dual.
I shall now proclaim the method for generating the gāthā:
Abiding in the contemplation of the mind and intellect,
The three karmas of the Tathāgata transform into the vajra-sharp syllable Oṃ, Which is able to sever all suffering and affliction.
Mañjuśrī, the Great Auspicious One, who proclaims the secret gateway through the subtle observation of wisdom—
homage to the Buddha, the World-Honored One, Sovereign King of Divine Mantras, from whom the wisdom of bodhi arises.
The syllable EṬ is the center of all things; it gives rise to the meaning of the Great and Supreme, and to great sentient beings.
It is free from mind, free from the characteristics of speech, and free from all sounds; it is the characteristic of all luminosity.
This great, great greed— All sentient beings are attached to it;
Great, great hatred is the cause of all suffering and affliction;
Great, great ignorance has deeply entered the minds of sentient beings.
Mahā-krodha (Great Wrath), he is the Great Harm;
Mahā-rati (Great Delight), he is the Great Attachment of the mind to various visions;
Mahā-kāma (Great Desire) and Mahā-sukha (Great Bliss); Mahā-harṣa (Great Joy) and Mahā-rañjana (Great Passion).
Great in form and great in body, Great in marks, great in appearance, great in name,
and great in giving; Holding the great mandala of perfect completion,
You wield the sword of great wisdom To sever the great web of afflictions.
Great Manifestation and Great Renown, Great Light and Great Radiance;
The Great Illusionist who creates illusions, Who accomplishes the meaning of great illusion;
The Great Illusory Emanation of Passion, The Great Illusory Net of Vision.
Supreme in great generosity, embraced by great ethical discipline,
upheld by great patience, valiant in great diligence,
abiding in great meditative concentration, and giving birth to great wisdom.
Great skillful means and great vows, Great power and great wisdom;
Great compassion and the selflessness of phenomena, Profound and wondrous conduct,
Great intelligence and great valor, Great giving and great skillful means.
Possessing the power of great supernormal knowledge, Of great majesty, valor,
and great blazing strength; The great flow and severance,
the great vajra secret, The great wrathful and fierce one.
The Great One who can remove all terrors, the Great and Supreme Vidyārāja,
the highest practice of the Mahāyāna; the one who increases the growth of the Mahāyāna Dharma,
the Buddha Mahāvairocana, the Great Silent Sage.
Born from the Great Mantra Section, Accomplishing the Secret Dharma by relying on the ten pāramitās,
One cultivates the sublime practices and attains the ten pāramitās—
This is the gateway to the pure and wondrous Dharma.
The ten kinds of pāramitās, The Tathāgata’s primordial true wisdom,
The sovereign practice of the ten stages, Abiding securely in the ten stages,
The pure body of the ten knowledges, The accumulation of the merits of the ten knowledges.
Ten aspects and ten benefits; the Honored One of the Ten Powers, the Muni, possesses vast conduct of ten aspects.
The Tathāgata’s pure body is entirely and universally perfected—neither real nor false.
Speaking truth and speaking reality, speaking as it is and not otherwise,
neither dual nor non-dual; abiding in the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*),
dwelling in the meaning of selflessness— this is like the lion’s roar.
His majesty shakes all non-Buddhists, and all demons are struck with terror;
he practices the conduct of universal emptiness, which the Tathāgata has personally realized.
With valor he destroys his enemies; thus he is named the Most Victorious One.
The Great Powerful Wheel-Turning King, the most supreme and honored one,
inspires a heart of reverence in all; realizing that phenomena are without distinction,
he expounds the Mahāyāna teachings and praises their boundless meaning.
The Tathāgata speaks words of truth, Neither real nor unreal,
yet he guides all deluded multitudes, Causing both śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas To attain the fruit of bodhi through the Buddha-vehicle.
Thoroughly understanding through reality that all things are empty and unattached,
the Arhat whose taints are exhausted has transcended desire and the supreme objects of the senses;
having ended all fetters of affliction, he has attained fearlessness and cool serenity.
The Tathāgata is free from attachment; he is the one perfected in knowledge and conduct,
the Well-Gone One, the Supreme Being in the world, the Tamer, the Honored One among the ten titles—
free from egoism and arrogance, his mind dwelling securely in reality.
Having distanced himself from saṃsāra, having completed all that was to be done through the cultivation of sublime practices for billions of eons,
the World-Honored One, the Great Dharma King whose mind of wisdom is resolute, proclaims the subtle and wondrous Dharma.
Pervading throughout the world, you teach and transform all sentient beings through most excellent conduct; accomplishing every benefit and purpose,
you act as a great guide, causing them to be free from all doubt.
Throughout the entire realm of sentient beings, may they all attain the ground of peace and security.
Through the cultivation of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, and meditative concentration, one creates a treasury of merit;
through the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom, one creates a treasury of knowledge.
Through skillful means and the power of vows, they follow and cultivate the practices that perfect the two collections;
their minds are always universally associated with subtle meditative concentration, manifesting bodily forms while remaining unmoving.
The three bodies of Dharma, Reward, and Transformation; The five Buddhas and their five kinds of wisdom;
The five Buddhas adorning the precious crown; The five eyes illuminating the world;
Manifesting as all Buddhas according to need; Causing the virtues of all beings to increase.
The power of wisdom cultivated through practice can sever all cycles of saṃsāra;
The Vairocana Buddha, whose body is as firm and solid as a vajra, Is the reality of inconceivable wisdom, blazing with the light of great insight.
Spontaneously from the midst of empty space, The light of wisdom surges forth,
illuminating all buddha-fields. This Great Divine Mantra of the Vidyārāja,
the body of all Tathāgatas, Fully accomplishes the ultimate truth.
With a great uṣṇīṣa, he universally radiates pure light that illumines the bodies of all Buddhas;
those Buddhas all look up at him with reverence and joy, their majestic deportment fully perfected.
I offer worship and extend praise to the Great Sage, the Muni,
who abides in the mantras of the three families; to the manifest presence of the samaya-mantras,
the most supreme among the Three Jewels, and to the Three Vehicles and their guides.
Amoghapāśakula: Holding the vajra-noose and the vajra-hook, manifesting a wrathful form to subjugate all māras and enemies; the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja.
Six faces manifesting six eyes, a single body arising with six arms,
and from the mouth protruding great fangs; holding a *khaṭvāṅga* in hand and with a hundred venomous snakes coiled around the arms— this is named Yamāntaka.
Also named King of Obstacle-Removal, manifesting a form of great terror,
he wields a sharp vajra blade; through various distinct manifestations,
he transforms the vajra retinue, filling the entirety of space.
The Great Ritual-Virtue Wrathful One, the Vidyārāja Acala,
with a single topknot of disheveled hair, draped in an elephant hide,
lets out a great laugh, the sound of "ha ha hi hi."
All plants and trees tremble; The Manifestation of the Great Laughing Vidyārāja possesses great majestic power.
Vajramahābodhisattva, Vajrarāja Mahāsukha, Vajralakṣaṇa Mahāharṣa.
Vajra mantra: Hūṃ hūṃ! Holding a vajra bow and arrow and a vajra sword, you sever all afflictions;
you are firm and efficacious—this is the most supreme Vajra.
Blazing with vajra flames, blazing with vajra eyes,
possessing the great form of the vajra; with a hundred vajra eyes and vajra hairs as sharp as razors, he manifests the appearance of battle.
The vajra manifests as fingernails, with billions of sharp and keen points;
the supreme garland of vajras, the wondrous adornment of vajras,
and the vajra sound of laughter— these are the six kinds of letter-gates.
Mañjuśrī’s great voice pervades the three realms and extends even to the realm of empty space; knowing that all sounds thus pervade everywhere,
one realizes that all phenomena are without self.
Transcending words and language, identical to the reality-limit and the nature of phenomena,
like a great bull-king, he roars with a mighty sound,
blowing the great conch of Dharma and beating the great drum of Dharma.
Raising the great banner of Dharma, Producing a vast sound,
you do not abide in nirvāṇa; Out of compassion for all sentient beings throughout the realms of space in the ten directions— Whether formless or non-formless.
Within the mind of manifold colors, one is able to comprehend all phenomena as being like a great,
perfect mirror; illuminating everything without exception,
they transform the multitudes of devas and humans, attaining mastery over the three realms.
Abiding in the noble path of equanimity, he emerges from the banner of the Dharma throughout the realms of the ten directions;
he manifests in the form of a youth, or in the form of a śramaṇa, or in the form of an old man.
Possessing the thirty-two marks, most sublime and exquisite in their dignity,
endowed with wisdom and virtuous conduct— may the Ācārya Dharma Master deliver all sentient beings and,
in accord with reality, attain perfect enlightenment.
Thoroughly comprehending the realm of space, with the ocean of omniscient wisdom,
you destroy the net of ignorance; you shatter the wheel of saṃsāra and forever leave behind all afflictions, swiftly reaching the further shore.
Consecrated with the water of wisdom, adorned with a sublime jewel crown,
he severed the three kinds of suffering, was liberated from all fetters,
and attained the state of Perfectly Complete Enlightenment.
Constantly within the three realms, you benefit all sentient beings;
Your pure conduct is perfected and your merits fully increased.
Free from all attachments, you dwell securely in the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*).
Holding the great wish-fulfilling jewel, you manifest as the supreme guide in accordance with the great signs; acting as the supreme auspicious vase,
you benefit all sentient beings and protect them as if they were your own infants.
Purity and non-purity, the samādhi of time, and the thorough penetration of correct concentration;
the penetration of the faculties of beings, the penetration of objects, the penetration of qualities,
and the penetration of dharmas— through these, one attains the three kinds of liberation.
Pure and auspicious, with a heart of joyful exultation;
five faces and five crowns, adorned by the five mountains;
the aspect of great joy and great bliss, great celebration and great desire.
The definitive true Dharma, the auspicious, most supreme,
and most excellent subtle conduct; for the benefit of all sentient beings,
to subdue the hosts of Māra and enemies, and to eliminate all terrors.
Śikhin Śramaṇa, Jaṭila, Lūhacīrin, and the Tāpasa;
those clad in the robes of great purity,
upholding the supreme Brahma-conduct— the assembly of Great Brahmins.
The Gautama who has reduced his body to ashes, having practiced great austerities,
has realized pure nirvāṇa; being tranquil, he has attained liberation and maintains the great conduct of purity, dwelling in bliss and free from attachment.
Having definitively severed pleasure and pain, having exhausted and distanced oneself from all desires,
without loss and without gain, without manifestation and without attachment,
with all conditioned formations free from defilement— such a one is called a brahmin.
The Bodhisattva practices correct conduct; his mental consciousness is pure, stainless, free from defilement, and without fear.
Having perfectly awakened to the Buddha-nature, he understands the wisdom of the Tathāgata-stage and is able to know all past phenomena.
There is neither ignorance nor form, nor is there any doubt;
I clearly perceive the Buddhas of the three periods of time. The Dharma is fundamentally without attachment;
awakening to this Dharma, one is freed from all fetters. With the eye of wisdom, one perceives without obstruction.
The Tathāgata’s wondrous wisdom contemplates; the Sovereign King of Dharma Exposition, by means of the most supreme dharma and meaning, completely eliminates all contentious arguments.
Like a lion king, he is able to subdue all the beasts.
All sentient beings look up with joyful reverence at the Tathāgata’s marks of honor;
Mañjuśrī’s light of wondrous wisdom blazes forth, illuminating everywhere;
The Crown Prince of the Dharma, the most supreme teacher of names and meanings.
Able to act as a great and excellent medicine, Eliminating all sufferings of illness;
Extending the light from the white ūrṇā-kośa, It illuminates the three realms and even the lands of the ten directions, Universally erecting the great banner of Dharma.
And spreading wide the great parasol, as the lotus great jewel canopy of the compassionate maṇḍala,
it universally covers the nature of all Buddhas’ dharmas and corresponds with all Buddhas.
Equal to all Buddhas, he is the most supreme and honored one;
the consecration of vajra-wisdom, the auspicious sovereign lord,
the master of all worlds, the most supreme Vajra King.
The Great Mind of all Buddhas, The Wisdom-Activity of all Buddhas,
The Great Body of all Buddhas, The Vajra-Sun of Great Radiance of the Sublime Eloquence of all Buddhas, The Vajra-Moon of Great Luminosity.
Blazing and illuminating everywhere throughout the realms of sentient beings in the ten directions;
the Buddha, firm as a vajra; the Buddha, born from the supreme dharma;
the Buddha, the auspicious lotus; the one who accomplishes all-knowledge.
The Buddha upholds the great illusory dharma; the Buddha upholds the great vidyā-mantra, the adamantine sword of great benefit.
It severs all fetters of affliction, the great vessel of the adamantine dharma, the most supreme adamantine dharma.
Born of Vajra-wisdom, adorned with the Buddha-ground of perfected pāramitās,
with a mind clearly illuminated by the pure right-knowledge of the selflessness of phenomena, one perceives the manifold events of the illusory net.
The Vajra is able to sever and eliminate afflictions until none remain.
*Mañjuśrī-paripṛcchā-nāmasaṃgīti*, Upper Scroll.
*Mañjuśrī-paripṛcchā-nāmasaṃgīti*, Lower Scroll.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master from the Western Heaven Mingyin Miaoshan Pujie,
Dharma Master Jintongchi, and others, by Imperial Decree:
The Body of the Bodhisattva’s Sublime Wisdom, which gives rise to all manner of virtuous benefits.
Just as from within the great earth, Various benefits arise—
the treasury of all buddha-wisdom— From which flows forth the Great Dharma Wheel,
the self-nature of all phenomena; All self-natures are thus produced.
In a single instant, one gives rise to the meaning of all phenomena and immediately attains great wisdom; awakening to the nature of all dharmas,
one enters deeply into various samādhis and abides in the principle of equality.
All phenomena are utterly pure; The perfectly awakened Buddhas appear before one.
Accomplishing the meaning of joy, The light of the flame of great wisdom Extinguishes all stains of sin.
Among all sentient beings, you act for their supreme benefit;
taking suffering as your enemy, your wisdom is victorious in battle.
You possess the marks of supreme diligence and sublime, wondrous, great auspiciousness.
His arms are a hundred cubits long; lifting his feet, he leaves no footprint.
With one foot he presses upon the Golden Wheel, while the other reaches down to the very limit of the earth;
with one foot he covers the Brahma-heaven, yet only his fingernails are visible.
Supreme, victorious, and sovereign, you manifest various forms and signs without differentiating between the Dharma and its meaning; arising from the wisdom of skillful means,
you pervade the realms of the ten directions, bringing benefit that is inexhaustible.
Having already departed from the defilements of saṃsāra,
you have attained the three great blisses like a pure cloud; you are like the bright autumn moon and like the sun freed from clouds, a blazing and magnificent radiance.
The great blue jewel of Śakra, of supreme and most excellent color,
as well as the great cintāmaṇi— through the power of the supernatural manifestations of these wondrous ornaments, a hundred worlds are shaken.
Abiding in the foundations of mindfulness and right efforts, with the bases of power, faculties, and powers,
and the exquisite flowers of the seven factors of awakening; understanding the eightfold noble path that leads to perfect enlightenment— this is the ocean of the Tathāgata’s virtues.
The aggregates of all sentient beings are like space;
The mental activities of all sentient beings, And the various distinctions of their faculties and objects,
Are known to be such that the five aggregates are entirely empty.
The meaning of the five aggregates is pure; having realized that all conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*) are beyond measure, one understands their characteristics.
Abiding within the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the nature of the twelve links of dependent origination is entirely pure.
The four immeasurables and the true vehicle; The eight knowledges arising from awakening, which produce internal faculties and external objects;
The twelvefold secret meaning of reality and the sixteen divisions; And the twenty kinds of the path of awakening.
In this way, the Buddhas fully realize this supreme truth;
manifesting countless bodies, they always abide in samādhi,
perceiving the mental activities of all sentient beings in a single instant.
The gateway of skillful means of the three vehicles,
The subtle awakening to the dharmas of pure conduct being without self-nature, Abiding in the path of the single vehicle,
exhausting all fetters of affliction, And emerging from the ocean of suffering of saṃsāra.
Having escaped the dense forest of fetters, through the wisdom of skillful means regarding various sufferings and great compassion,
you are able to universally benefit and sustain all sentient beings,
causing them to realize the patience of non-arising.
The minds of all sentient beings are understood as pure realms;
The minds of all sentient beings are equal and without distinction;
The minds of all sentient beings give rise to joy and loving attachment.
Causing one to be free from distraction, To accomplish all merits and penetrate the dharmas of the three periods of time;
The meaning of all wisdom is that the nature of the five aggregates is fundamentally empty— All three periods of time are thus.
In a single thought, one gives rise to faith and understanding, And immediately perceives the nature of all Buddhas.
The self-nature of all phenomena arises; The Buddha-body is fundamentally without attachment.
One joyfully beholds the bodies of all Buddhas, Adorned with manifold marks of excellence.
Delighting in hearing the Buddha’s bodhi, the supreme and true meaning;
The great mantra that transcends words, the great mantra in which the three natures are extinguished and seen as wordless; It gives birth to all mantras.
The hundred-gate door of *mindu*, the five-gate doors, and the sixteen kinds of the secret of Great Emptiness (*mahāśūnyatā*);
from within *mindu* arise *kṣara* and *akṣara*; in the past, there were four kinds.
The meaning of dhyāna arises in billions of ways; he penetrates all that is conditioned and unconditioned.
He fully understands the fundamental concentrations and samādhis, his body being supreme;
so too are his reward and transformation bodies.
Pervading the realms of the ten directions, He transforms and delivers all sentient beings.
The final God among Gods, the most auspicious and supreme,
He is the guide for devas and humans, Who has subdued the hosts of Māras.
Like Śakra, King of Devas, you are able to perform great acts of giving to deliver all sentient beings; emerging from the dense forest of afflictions,
you are praised throughout the ten directions— unique and without a second.
With the dharma of great compassion as his armor of diligence,
and wisdom as his bow and sword, he utterly destroys the thieves of affliction;
by his most supreme and majestic spiritual power, all māras are struck with fear.
Having subdued the hosts of Māra and enemies, I offer vast and extensive worship.
I bow my head to the Supreme Teacher, To the Buddhas who protect the world;
With prostrations and praise, I draw near and serve them.
In the empty realms of the ten directions, the offerings are likewise thus.
Mañjuśrī, the Great Auspicious One, is a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who possesses the six supernormal powers and the three clarities, and whose six recollections are all perfected.
Manifesting great supernormal powers, With wisdom reaching the further shore,
far removed from saṃsāra, Forever attaining non-retrogression through courageous and great diligence, Thoroughly understanding all phenomena.
The Great Person, having attained transcendence of the supreme stages,
universally moistens all sentient beings with the rain of Dharma through wisdom,
proclaims the four seals of the Dharma, and guides them toward the three vehicles.
The pure and supreme meaning, Capable of bringing about great auspiciousness,
praised by Bodhisattvas; To the Vajra Honored One,
who brings accomplishment to countless beings, I look up with reverence and pay homage.
I take refuge in the Great Treasury of Space; I praise the Great Treasury of Space.
I take refuge in the Buddha’s path of awakening; I praise the Buddha’s path of awakening.
I take refuge in the bodies of all Buddhas; I praise the bodies of all Buddhas.
I take refuge in the Buddha with joy; I praise the Buddha with joy.
I take refuge in the virtues of the Buddha; I praise the virtues of the Buddha.
I take refuge in the mindfulness of all Buddhas; I praise the mindfulness of all Buddhas.
I take refuge in the Buddha’s joyful smile; I praise the Buddha’s joyful smile.
I take refuge in the speech of all Buddhas; I praise the speech of all Buddhas.
I take refuge in that which is beloved by the Buddha; I praise that which is beloved by the Buddha.
I take refuge in those born from the Buddhas; I praise those born from the Buddhas.
I take refuge in those born from the Buddha’s wisdom; I praise those born from the Buddha’s wisdom.
I take refuge in the Buddha’s dance; I praise the Buddha’s dance.
I take refuge in the Omniscient One; I praise the emptiness of the nature of omniscience and the Net of Illusion. My refuge and praise are likewise thus.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi—
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One,
the Tathāgata’s wisdom-contemplation of the body of all-knowledge is profoundly deep and subtle."
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī,
desiring to benefit all sentient beings,
has spoken this pure and most excellent exposition of names and meanings.
If there are sentient beings whose three karmas are not yet purified,
may they be caused to grasp and maintain the three karmas within the treasury of merit and wisdom—
the gateway to the perfections of the Buddha-ground— so that they become perfectly pure.
To cause those who have not yet understood the supreme meaning to attain understanding,
and even for all the Dharma-treasuries of the Buddhas,
to open them up so that they may be awakened to and comprehend them.
It gives birth to all virtues as a gateway to merit.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi said:

"This most excellent name and meaning gives birth to all pure stages, pāramitās, dharmas, and secret mantras; it perfectly accomplishes the ocean of all meritorious qualities of the knowledge of all-knowledge."
Purifying the three secrets of body, speech, and mind,
one visualizes all the Buddhas, the Truly and Completely Enlightened Ones,
and accomplishes the Great Samādhi of Buddha-wisdom.
The pure dharma-realm of all Tathāgatas,
possessing the most supreme ten powers that destroy the enmity of Māra,
and endowed with all-knowledge and the knowledge of all modes.
The fundamental skillful means benefit all sentient beings;
it is a treasury of merit and wisdom, pure and perfect,
giving birth to bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas.
The noble lineages of the two vehicles, all humans and devas,
and those bodhisattvas who abide in Mahāyāna practices,
having entered the true holy path, shall all attain liberation.
Furthermore, it can increase the bodhisattva’s roots of goodness,
subdue all heterodox and divergent doctrines, and through its majestic power,
crush and subjugate the four kinds of māra-enemies.
May all sentient beings together return to the noble path;
may they be liberated from their bonds and free from all distraction,
becoming fully endowed with every virtuous undertaking.
Having severed the cycle of saṃsāra and attained the true path of the noble ones,
one universally makes offerings to all Tathāgatas with exquisite incense, flowers, banners, pennants, parasols, and canopies.
One will swiftly attain accomplishment in all the gateways of mantras,
conceive a sense of affection and joy toward all bodhisattvas,
and become correspondingly associated with the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
They thoroughly understand that the bodhisattva’s practice of emptiness is non-dual;
they are fully endowed with the treasury of all pāramitās and have perfected all the pure stages of Buddhahood.
The noble wisdom of the Four Noble Truths manifests before them;
they dwell with single-minded concentration in the four foundations of mindfulness,
until they are fully endowed with all the merits of the Buddhas.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi said:
"This *Sūtra of the Most Victorious Names and Meanings* can eliminate all the impurities of unwholesome karma of body, speech, and mind belonging to all sentient beings."
May they be enabled to remain far removed from all evil realms,
attain the severance of all karmic obstructions,
and have all fears of the eight difficulties completely eliminated.
One shall be free from evil dreams and attain great auspiciousness;
furthermore, one shall be liberated from all demonic adversaries and fetters,
and cultivate the roots of goodness, merit, and benefit.
He has severed all forms of overweening pride (*adhimāna*),
forever departed from the cycle of suffering and rebirth,
and possesses the realization of the minds of all Buddhas as they truly are, as well as the realization of the secret conduct of Bodhisattvas as it truly is.
The noble wisdom of the three vehicles understands reality as it truly is;
all mantras and mudrās understand reality as it truly is;
and the supreme meaning of the Dharma gives rise to great wisdom.
